metaTitle: Best Benchtop Band Saws for Woodworking (2026)
metaDescription: Benchtop band saws compared by resaw height, throat width, motor type, blade speeds and table size, so you can match a saw to curves, resawing and small shops.
expertTake: The Rikon 10-3062S is the best benchtop band saw for most hobbyists because of its 5 inch cut height, two speeds and tool-less guides. The WEN BA3959 is the value pick for curves in thin stock. The WEN BA3962 is the choice if you want a 6 inch resaw capacity and a stand. If you mostly cut straight lines in sheet goods, a table saw or track saw is a better buy.
introParagraphs: A band saw is a continuous blade stretched over two wheels. It cuts curves, resaws thick boards into thin ones and makes cuts a table saw cannot, because the blade never kicks back at the operator. Benchtop models bring that capacity to small shops and garages.

The numbers on the box, like amps and throat size, do not tell you how well a saw tracks or resaws. This guide explains the specs that decide results, then points you to the top picks above and the reviews below.

products.name: RIKON 10-3062S 10 in Deluxe Band Saw with Stand
products.description:
The Rikon 10-3062S is a 10 inch saw with a 1/2 horsepower motor, two blade speeds of 1,515 and 3,280 feet per minute, and a 5 inch cut height. The slow speed suits thicker stock, plastics and soft metals, and the fast speed suits wood. It takes blades up to 1/2 inch wide, so it can resaw as well as cut curves.

Tool-less guides are the feature that separates it from the budget saws. Guide adjustment is the main source of frustration on a benchtop saw, and setting them by hand saves time. Compared with the DeWalt 9 inch model at 3.5 amps and a 9 inch throat, the Rikon gives more cut height and a bigger stand-based footprint, though it costs noticeably more.

The stand makes the saw steadier and reduces vibration. Replace the tires when they crack and check blade tracking after each change. The stand-mounted motor makes it a shop fixture rather than a tool you carry.
products.bestFor: Hobbyists who want a refined benchtop saw that can resaw and cut curves.
pros: Two blade speeds cover wood and softer metals
5 inch cut height allows real resawing
cons: Priced above every other benchtop saw here
Stand and footprint need dedicated shop space

products.name: WEN BA3959 9 in 2.8 Amp Benchtop Band Saw
products.description:
The WEN BA3959 is a 9 inch benchtop saw with a 2.8 amp motor that turns the blade up to 2,500 feet per minute. It cuts up to 3-1/2 inches deep and 9 inches wide and accepts 59-1/2 inch blades from 1/8 to 3/8 inch wide.

That capacity suits small projects, curves in 3/4 inch stock and craft work, but it is not a resaw machine. A 3-1/2 inch cut height limits you to boards about that thick, whereas the WEN BA3962 reaches 6 inches. It is among the least expensive saws in the lineup, so it is a sensible way to learn how a band saw behaves before investing in a larger machine.

Expect to spend time on setup. Check blade tracking and tension, set the guides and square the table to the blade. Replace the stock blade with a quality one if you cut hardwood.
products.bestFor: Beginners cutting curves in thin stock on a small budget.
pros: Low cost of entry for a 9 inch saw
3-1/2 inch depth handles most craft stock
cons: Not suited to resawing thick boards
Stock blade and guides need setup care

products.name: WEN BA3962 10 in 3.5 Amp Band Saw with Stand
products.description:
The BA3962 pairs a 3.5 amp two-speed motor with a 10 inch throat and a 6 inch cut height. It uses a 72 inch blade up to 1/2 inch wide and has a 14-1/8 by 12-1/2 inch cast aluminum table that bevels to 45 degrees.

The 6 inch height is the largest in this guide, matching the VEVOR but beating the Rikon at 5 inches. A bigger table helps support long boards, and a 1/2 inch blade will track straighter for resawing. As a package with a stand, it costs less than the Rikon but lacks its tool-less guide system.

A saw with a 3.5 amp motor needs a sharp, properly tensioned blade to resaw cleanly. Check that the stand bolts are tight, since vibration loosens them.
products.bestFor: Woodworkers who need the deepest cut at a moderate cost.
pros: Takes blades up to 1/2 inch wide
cons: Longer 72 inch blades cost more than 59-1/2 inch ones

products.name: SKIL BW9501-00 9 in 2.8 Amp 2-Speed Band Saw
products.description:
The SKIL BW9501 uses a 2.8 amp induction motor with a two-speed drive and a tool-free belt tensioning system. Induction motors run quieter and with less brush wear than universal motors, which suits a garage or basement shop.

It has a quick blade tension setting, which helps new users reach a repeatable tension. Compared with the WEN BA3959, which has a similar 2.8 amp rating, the SKIL adds two speeds and tool-free belt access. Capacity is similar to other 9 inch saws, so it fits curves and thin stock rather than resawing.

Change the belt position for slower speed when cutting plastics or thin material. Keep the blade clean to avoid pitch buildup, and verify the table is square.
products.bestFor: Quiet curve cutting in a home shop.
cons: Limited resaw capacity on a 9 inch frame
Fewer published capacity details than rivals

products.name: DeWalt 9 in 3.5 Amp Two-Speed Band Saw with LED
products.description:
The DeWalt 9 inch band saw has a 3.5 amp motor, two speeds of 1,700 and 2,500 strokes per minute and an integrated LED that lights the cutting line. Light on the line is a practical help when you follow a pencil mark through a curve.

It is aimed at hobby and light work, and the 3.5 amp rating is higher than the 2.8 amp motors in the SKIL and WEN BA3959. The spec sheet is thin compared with the Rikon, so check cut height and table size before buying.

Two speeds let you slow down for thin stock and plastics. As with any benchtop saw, tension and guide setup determine cut quality more than the badge.
products.bestFor: Hobbyists who value a lit cutting line and a trusted tool brand.
pros: Built-in LED lights the cut line
cons: Resaw capacity limited by 9 inch frame
Less detailed capacity data than rivals

products.name: SHOPMAX 4.2 Amp 10 in Benchtop Band Saw
products.description:
The SHOPMAX has a 4.2 amp induction motor, the highest amp rating among the induction saws in this guide, with a 10 inch throat and a 4.5 inch cut height. It takes 67.4 inch blades from 0.14 to 0.47 inch wide, and the table tilts to 45 degrees.

The 4.2 amp motor gives it more headroom for resawing than the 2.8 amp SKIL, and the 4.5 inch height sits between the WEN BA3959 at 3-1/2 and the BA3962 at 6 inches. A 67.4 inch blade length is not standard, so confirm blade availability before you commit.

Induction motors are low maintenance, and the main upkeep is tires, bearings and guides. Quick table angle adjustment makes bevel cuts easier.
products.bestFor: Woodworkers who want a quiet motor with extra power for resawing.
cons: Brand has a shorter track record

buyingCriteria.explanation: Cut height is the thickest board the saw can pass under the upper guide. The WEN BA3959 gives 3-1/2 inches, the SHOPMAX 4.5, the Rikon 5 and the WEN BA3962 6. Resawing a 6 inch board into veneers needs the full height, and many buyers pick a saw by throat width and find it too short.

Induction motors, like those in the SKIL BW9501 and SHOPMAX, run quieter and need no brushes. Amps run from 2.8 on the WEN BA3959 to 4.2 on the SHOPMAX. More power helps when the blade is wide and the wood is dense, but a sharp blade matters more than motor size.

Wood cuts best near 2,500 feet per minute, as on the WEN BA3959 and WOODSKIL class saws. Slower speeds suit plastics and soft metals. The Rikon offers 1,515 and 3,280 FPM, and the DeWalt offers 1,700 and 2,500 strokes per minute.

Guides keep the blade from twisting, and poor guides ruin cuts. The Rikon has tool-less guides, while budget saws like the WEN BA3959 need a wrench. Set the guides about a credit card thickness from the blade and check tracking by hand-turning the wheel.

Blade length is fixed by the frame. The WEN BA3959 uses 59-1/2 inch blades, the BA3962 72 inch, and the SHOPMAX 67.4 inch. Standard lengths are easier to find. A narrow 1/8 inch blade cuts tight curves, while a 1/2 inch blade resaws straighter.

A 14-1/8 by 12-1/2 inch table, like the WEN BA3962, supports long boards better than a small one. Most tables tilt to 45 degrees, and the VEVOR tilts 5 degrees left too. Check that the table is flat and square to the blade out of the box.

specDecoder.meaning: Throat is the distance from the blade to the frame. A 9 inch throat limits the width of a board you can cut in the middle of a panel. A 10 inch throat gives about 9-3/4 inches of cut width.
specDecoder.watchFor: Throat is not cut height. A 10 inch saw can still resaw only 4.5 inches, like the SHOPMAX.

specDecoder.meaning: Cut height is the clearance under the upper blade guide. It decides the thickest stock you can pass. Capacity is lower at 45 degrees table tilt.
specDecoder.watchFor: Some listings quote the maximum with the guide raised fully, which is unsafe in practice. Expect a lower safe height.

specDecoder.meaning: Feet per minute describes the blade travel speed, and strokes per minute is a looser term used on some listings. Wood runs best around 2,500 FPM, and softer metals need slower speeds.
specDecoder.watchFor: A saw advertised at 3,280 FPM is faster, not better. Match speed to material.

specDecoder.meaning: An induction motor uses no brushes and runs quieter with long life. It is usually paired with a belt drive. The SKIL and SHOPMAX use them.
specDecoder.watchFor: Amp ratings between induction and universal motors are not directly comparable.

specDecoder.meaning: Blade length is the loop circumference, and the frame sets it. A 59-1/2 inch blade fits the WEN BA3959, 72 inch fits the BA3962.
specDecoder.watchFor: A nonstandard length limits your choice of blades and raises replacement cost.

howWeEvaluated.title: Resaw capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked each saw by cut height first, from 3-1/2 inches on the WEN BA3959 to 6 inches on the WEN BA3962. Cut height decides whether a saw can resaw, and it is the spec buyers most often misjudge.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor and drive
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared induction and universal designs, amp ratings and speed options. The SHOPMAX at 4.2 amps and the Rikon at 1/2 horsepower sit at the top, and the two 2.8 amp saws sit at the bottom.

howWeEvaluated.title: Guides and setup
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at whether guides adjust without tools and how simple blade tension is to set. The Rikon led here, and the SKIL has a quick tension setting.

howWeEvaluated.title: Table and stand
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked table size, tilt range and whether a stand comes in the box. The WEN BA3962 and Rikon include stands, which reduces vibration.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blade supply
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked blade lengths because replacement cost is an ownership expense. Standard sizes like 59-1/2 and 72 inches score better than unusual lengths such as 67.4 inches.

cards.label: Induction
cards.text: Induction motors run quieter and last longer with no brushes. The SKIL BW9501 and SHOPMAX use this type, which suits a shared garage.

cards.label: Universal
cards.text: Universal motors are lighter and cheaper but louder. Treat the amp rating as a rough guide only.

howToChoose.note: Pick induction for quiet shops and universal for lowest cost.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for at least 5 inches of cut height, a wide blade and a stable frame. A narrow blade will wander in thick stock.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The WEN BA3962 at 6 inches and the Rikon at 5 inches are the two serious resaw options.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more on the RIKON 10-3062S if you will use guides daily and cut thick stock.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save with the WEN BA3959 if you cut curves in thin stock occasionally.

maintenance.why: Poor tension makes the blade wander. Track the blade on the wheel crown by hand.
Guides prevent twist. Too tight causes heat, too loose lets the blade drift.
Leaving tension on stretches the blade and flattens wheel tires. Release it after long sessions.
Pitch and dust cause tracking problems. Wipe the tires and brush the wheels.
A dull blade wanders and heats. A new blade fixes most cutting complaints.

faq.q: Is a 9 inch or 10 inch band saw better?
faq.a: A 10 inch saw usually offers a larger table and more cut height. A 9 inch saw is lighter and suits curve cutting. Check cut height rather than the throat label.

faq.q: Can a benchtop band saw resaw hardwood?
faq.a: Yes, if it has at least 5 inches of cut height and a sharp wide blade. Slow feed rates and a fence help.
Two speeds help if you cut plastics, thin stock or soft metals. For wood alone, one speed near 2,500 FPM works.

faq.q: What blade should I buy first?
faq.a: A 1/4 inch blade with 6 teeth per inch is a good general starter. Use narrower blades for tight curves and wider ones for resawing.
Drift comes from a dull blade, poor tracking or misaligned guides. Fix those before blaming the saw.

faq.q: Can I cut metal on a wood band saw?
faq.a: Only soft metals at slow speed with the right blade. A dedicated metal band saw is a better tool for steel.
